display.text: Limiting reference distribution approached as sample size increases; the regular LRT uses an asymptotic chi-square distribution.
Difference in the numbers of freely estimated parameters between the full and restricted models, used for the regular asymptotic chi-square reference.

response.correctResponse: degrees of freedom for an LRT

display.text: Function of model parameters that evaluates how well those parameter values support the observed data under the model.
Natural logarithm of the likelihood, used to compare model fits and calculate likelihood ratio statistics.
Numerical criterion measuring prediction error that a fitting algorithm seeks to reduce, such as squared error or cross-entropy.
Parameter estimation that selects values making the observed data most likely under the specified statistical model.
Average squared prediction error, Σ(Yᵢ − Ŷᵢ)²/n, in squared response units. This prediction metric uses n, unlike residual mean squares in inferential ANOVA tables. Abbreviated MSE.
Degree to which a model's predictions agree with observed data and capture relevant patterns.
Choice of variables, functional form, and distributional structure defining a statistical model.
Models in which the simpler model is obtained by imposing restrictions on parameters of the more general model.
Coefficient-fitting method that minimizes the sum of squared residuals.
Addition of a model-complexity penalty to a fitting objective to restrain overfitting, as in ridge and lasso regression.
Sum of squared differences between observed responses and their fitted values, measuring variation left unexplained by a model. Notation: SSres.
Square root of prediction MSE, expressing squared-error performance in the response's original units; smaller values indicate better predictions on comparable data. Abbreviated RMSE.
Mathematical representation of patterns in data used to explain, predict, or make inferences about outcomes.
Sum of squared deviations of observed responses from their mean, measuring total response variation. Notation: SStot.
Failure of an overly simple model to capture important patterns in the data.
